findings.current: “Then could you wake up Kkeokjeong Hyung-nim first?”
findings.defect: Song Song addresses Kkeokjeong as 아저씨, but the draft gives her Taekyung’s male junior-to-senior address, changing their relationship and her voice.
findings.rationale: The established alias “Uncle Kkeokjeong” preserves her distinct 아저씨 address without assigning her Taekyung’s Hyung-nim hierarchy.
findings.replacement: “Then could you wake Uncle Kkeokjeong first?”

findings.current: At the same time, more than twenty arrows infused with mana struck the head of the lead Minotaur.
findings.defect: “More than twenty” makes the quantity strictly greater than twenty, while 이십여 발 means approximately twenty.
findings.rationale: “Around twenty” preserves the source’s approximate quantity.
findings.replacement: At the same time, around twenty arrows infused with mana struck the head of the lead Minotaur.
findings.source: 동시에 마나를 머금은 이십여 발의 화살이 선두에 선 미노타우로스의 머리에 꽂혔다.

findings.current: Damn it. I’d been happy for nothing. That was just how my life went.
findings.defect: 좋다 말았네 means his excitement was abruptly cut short, not that his happiness had been baseless.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores the comic beat of anticipation being immediately spoiled and retains Taekyung’s self-deprecating register.
findings.replacement: Damn it. And just when I was getting excited. That was my life for you.
findings.source: 젠장. 좋다 말았네. 내 인생이 이렇지 뭐.

findings.current: Anyway, Miss Song had ordered hangover soup.
findings.defect: The plain statement omits the surprised, incongruous reaction conveyed by 라니.
findings.rationale: The source marks her choice as surprising before contrasting it with her pampered appearance.
findings.replacement: Still, I never would’ve expected Miss Song to order hangover soup.

findings.current: But what arrived on the table was a steaming bowl of haejangguk, a Korean soup traditionally eaten to ease a hangover.[^1]
findings.defect: The inline explanation duplicates footnote 1 and adds an expository gloss directly to the narration.
findings.rationale: The existing footnote already supplies the useful cultural explanation, so the reading copy should retain only the source’s reveal.
findings.replacement: But what arrived on the table was a steaming bowl of haejangguk.[^1]

findings.current: “Where else? We’ve got to keep the party going from yesterday. How about makgeolli today? I know a place that makes it well.”
findings.defect: The makgeolli footnote is left unreferenced, and “a place that makes it well” awkwardly suggests production rather than a good establishment.
findings.rationale: The replacement activates the existing cultural footnote and naturally renders 잘하는 집 as a place known for serving it well.
findings.replacement: “Where else? We’ve got to keep the party going from yesterday. How about makgeolli today?[^2] I know a good place.”
findings.source: “어디긴, 어제에 이어서 또 달려야지. 오늘은 막걸리 어때? 내가 잘하는 집 알아.”

summary: One hierarchy error, one altered quantity, two lost pragmatic cues, and two footnote-related issues are actionable.
